title: Permission and Procurement Guidance Hub
author: Aisha Khan
content:
Overview: This playbook consolidates company-wide standards and repeatable procedures for access and permissions, change management, data handling, procurement & expenses, vendor onboarding, and travel approvals. It is intended as the primary operational reference for managers, finance, security, and engineering teams. Scope: - Applies to all full-time employees, contractors, and approved third-party vendors interacting with Redwood systems or purchasing on behalf of the company. - Excludes ad-hoc personal travel not billed to Redwood and personal purchases without company reimbursement. Key objectives: - Reduce approval friction while preserving least-privilege access and compliance requirements. - Standardize procurement and vendor onboarding to improve cycle time and auditability. - Provide safe change management guardrails to protect production availability. - Ensure consistent data classification, retention, and handling across teams. Ownership and escalation: | Area | Primary owner | Secondary owner | Escalation contact | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Access & permissions | Identity & Security (security@redwood.com) | Eng SRE | it-ops@redwood.com | | Change management | Eng Platform | Eng SRE | oncall@redwood.com | | Data retention/classification | Data Governance (dgovern@redwood.com) | Legal | legal@redwood.com | | Procurement & vendor onboarding | Finance Procurement | Legal | procurement@redwood.com | | Travel & expenses | People Ops | Finance | travel@redwood.com | Access & Permissions: Principles: - Principle of least privilege: default to read-only and grant higher privileges for clearly documented business needs. - Time-bounded grants: every non-service access request must have an expiration <= 90 days unless renewed via documented review. - Separation of duties: critical actions (billing, secret rotation, production deploys) require at least two approvers from different teams. Request procedure (standard access): 1) Employee submits request in Access Portal with: justification, required roles, requested duration, and owner. 2) System owner (service/team owner) must approve within 48 business hours. If owner is unavailable, fallback approver is Eng SRE. 3) Identity & Security validates role-to-permission mapping and performs automated entitlement checks. 4) Request is provisioned and logged with a ticket reference. Emergency access (break glass): - For Severity 1 incidents where production is impaired, on-call SRE may grant scoped emergency access via the Break Glass procedure. Access must be time-limited to 4 hours and recorded in incident ticket. Post-incident retro must include a justification and entitlement review. Service accounts and API keys: - Must be registered in the Service Identity Registry and use short-lived credentials where supported (<=24h). - Secrets must be stored in KMS/vault (HashiCorp Vault or cloud KMS) and rotated at least quarterly. RBAC mapping guideline (example): - Viewer: read-only to telemetry, dashboards, tickets. - Developer: push to pre-prod branches, create feature flags, test infra. - Platform Operator: can deploy to production, restart services (requires 2FA and MFA). - Billing Admin: view and manage billing (separate from deploy privileges). Change Management: Change categories: - Routine: configuration changes with low risk (e.g., app config tweak). No CAB required if:
- change has automated canary and rollback, and
- no schema migration, and
- scheduled in non-peak window. - Standard: planned changes with medium risk. Requires peer review, automated tests, and a CAB notification (48 hours). - Major: schema migrations, infra changes, data migrations, or anything impacting SLA. Requires documented rollout plan, risk assessment, and CAB approval. CAB (Change Advisory Board) rules: - Weekly CAB meeting: Tuesdays 09:00-10:00 PT. Major changes must be submitted by Monday 17:00 PT to be reviewed. - CAB composition: Eng Platform lead, SRE oncall lead, Security rep, Product owner, and Finance rep when cost-impacting. - Rollout window: default production change window is 02:00–05:00 PT. Exceptions require documented risk and a fallback plan. Rollback and post-change verification: - Every standard/major change must include a rollback script and verification checklist with quantitative checkpoints (latency <= 1.25x baseline, error rate delta <= +0.5%). - Post-change review: owner must file a 72-hour review summary if any metric deviates more than threshold. Data Management: Classification levels: - Public: safe to publish externally (marketing collateral, public docs). Retention: as needed. - Internal: not public, limited to employees and contractors. Retention: 3 years standard. - Confidential: PII, customer data, contract terms. Retention: business need; default 7 years for legal/finance records. - Restricted: regulated data (HIPAA/PCI/financial personal data). Requires encryption at rest and in transit, and access must be limited and audited. Storage & handling: - Approved storage: S3 buckets in approved org accounts with bucket policies; encrypted with KMS; logging enabled. - Local disk: no sensitive data should be stored on developer laptops without approved disk encryption and device registration. - Backups: daily snapshots for critical datasets, 30-day hot retention with quarterly snapshots archived to long-term storage. Data retention and deletion process: 1) Data owner defines retention period in the Data Catalog. 2) Automated TTL jobs run nightly to flag expired data. 3) Deletion jobs run in a staging environment first; then in prod during a maintenance window. Procurement & Vendor Management: Procurement thresholds and approval matrix: - <$2,000: Team lead approval. Purchase via company card. - $2,000–$25,000: Department manager + Finance procurement approval. PO required. - $25,000–$250,000: VP-level approval + Legal review. PO + signed contract. - >$250,000: Executive committee approval + Legal and Security review. Competitive bids or Sole Source justification required. Vendor onboarding checklist (minimum): 1) Business justification and estimated TCO. 2) Legal: MSA or suitable contract, DPA if processing customer data. 3) Security: vendor risk assessment, required controls, penetration test evidence if applicable. 4) Finance: payment terms, tax information, and budget code. 5) Operations: connectivity requirements, SLA expectations, and escalation contacts. Vendor risk levels and required controls: - Low-risk: standard SaaS tools with no customer data. Controls: SOC2 Type II or equivalent recommended. - Medium-risk: vendors that process internal data or employee PII. Controls: DPA, encryption, and periodic security questionnaires. - High-risk: vendors that process customer data, financial, or regulated data. Controls: full security assessment, contractual security obligations, and periodic audits. Contracting and PO process (steps): 1) Raise PR in procurement system with budget code and vendor details. 2) Finance validates budget availability within 2 business days. 3) Legal reviews contract (7–10 business days typical). 4) Procurement issues PO and routes to vendor. 5) Vendor delivers and Finance reconciles invoice to PO before payment. Travel and Expense Policy (summary): Pre-approval: - All reimbursable travel must have manager pre-approval in Travel Portal with purpose, estimated cost, and dates. Allowable expenses & limits: - Flights: economy for trips <8 hours; premium economy only with VP approval. - Lodging: reasonable business-class hotels; per-night cap $250 in North America unless approved. - Meals: per diem $75/day in NA, $50/day in Europe. Itemized receipts required for amounts >$25. - Ground transport: rideshare/standard car or approved rental; personal car mileage reimbursed at company rate. Approval flow for expense reports: 1) Employee submits expenses in Expensify within 10 business days of travel with receipts. 2) Manager approves within 5 business days. 3) Finance performs spot-checks and processes reimbursement within the next payroll cycle. Non-reimbursable items: - Personal entertainment, in-room mini-bar overages without receipt justification, fines (parking/ticketing), and family travel unless previously authorized. Templates and examples (copy/paste ready): 1) Access request template: - requester: "[name]" - system: "[service-name]" - requested_role: "[Viewer|Developer|Operator]" - justification: "[business need]" - duration_days: "[30]" - owner: "[service-owner@example.com]" 2) Vendor onboarding checklist (short): - vendor_name: "[Vendor Inc]" - use_case: "[logging]" - risk_level: "[Low|Medium|High]" - legal_signed: "[yes/no]" - security_review_complete: "[yes/no]" 3) PO template (example): { "po_number": "PO-2025-0001", "vendor": "ExampleVendor, Inc.", "amount": "$12,500", "budget_code": "ENG-TOOLS-2025", "deliverables": "3-year SaaS subscription", "payment_terms": "Net 30" } Audit & evidence retention: - Procurement artifacts (POs, contracts, approvals) retained for 7 years. - Access logs for production systems retained for 365 days; security-relevant logs retained for 2 years by default. - Periodic audits: Internal audit performs a procurement and vendor control audit every 12 months. Operational metrics and targets (examples): - Access request SLA: 95% of standard requests approved within 48 business hours. - Vendor onboarding TAT: Low-risk vendor onboarding target = 7 business days. - Procurement PO issuance: 90% of POs issued within 5 business days after approval. Monitoring and continuous improvement: - Monthly cross-functional review meeting (Finance, Security, People Ops, Eng Platform) to review metrics, exceptions, and process improvements. - Runbook updates: owner teams must update relevant runbooks within 10 business days after any policy change. Related tools and links: - Access Portal: https://access.redwood.internal/ - Procurement system: https://procure.redwood.internal/ - Travel Portal: https://travel.redwood.internal/ - Service Identity Registry: https://services.redwood.internal/registry Appendix A — Quick decision trees (text): - Is vendor processing customer data? -> If yes, classify as Medium/High -> Engage Security and Legal before PO. - Does change touch production data schemas? -> If yes -> Major change -> CAB + rollback plan required. Appendix B — Contact list: - Identity & Security: security@redwood.com - Procurement: procurement@redwood.com - Finance (AP): ap@redwood.com - People Ops (travel): travel@redwood.com - Eng Platform lead: eng-platform@redwood.com Document maintenance: - This document is reviewed quarterly by Finance Procurement and Security. Any updates must be published with a change log entry. End of playbook.
